stem:
Veer has a square paper. He wants to count its lines of symmetry by testing folds.

Which two claims correctly count those lines?

options.text: Infinitely many, because any line through the centre looks balanced at a glance.
Four lines: two through midpoints of opposite sides and two through opposite corners, each passing the fold test.
Systematic fold checks find exactly four valid fold lines on the square.
Four folds are what create the square in the first place.

teacher.key_rationale: A square has four fold lines that each pass the overlap test. Glance balance omits the fold test. Saying folds create the square reverses the relation.
